subcategory: Southern Appalachian grassy bald native perennial legume

planting.note: Direct sow scarified, cold-stratified seed in fall, or divide established clumps in early spring; set plants in full sun with sharply drained soil mimicking its high-elevation bald habitat.

directions: Ash-leaved Golden-banner is a compact, clump-forming perennial legume confined to the grassy balds, rocky summits, and high-elevation openings of the southern Blue Ridge Mountains, where it sends up stiff stems of blue-green trifoliate leaves topped with bright yellow pea-flower racemes in late spring. It stays noticeably shorter and tidier than its lowland Piedmont relative Carolina Bush Pea, making it a good fit for sunny rock gardens and high-elevation native plantings that echo its open, fast-draining mountain turf. Start from scarified, cold-stratified seed sown outdoors in fall, or divide established rhizomatous clumps in early spring. It performs best where summers stay cool, and tends to decline in hot, humid lowland gardens far below its native elevation.
sources: Flora of the Southeastern United States (Weakley, UNC Herbarium) - Thermopsis fraxinifolia
